s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital cerebral and ocular abnormalities with prenatal and postnatal findings
salient_findings: Severe thinning of frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
key_facts: Born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
Weight at birth: 2152 g
One of monochorionic diamniotic twins
Identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound showed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI revealed microcephaly and marked enlargement of lateral ventricles
No signs of elevated intracranial pressure
Severe thinning of frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
Temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions
Very weak light reflexes bilaterally at 1 week of age
Mild optic nerve pallor
Fundus had a faint reddish tone
Retinal vessels appeared normal in caliber and reached the periphery

shortlist.label: Walker-Warburg syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by congenital muscular dystrophy, ocular malformations, and brain abnormalities, matching the case's prenatal and postnatal findings of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and ocular abnormalities

shortlist.label: Muscle-eye-brain disease
shortlist.why_kept: Involves congenital muscular dystrophy, eye abnormalities, and brain malformations, consistent with the case's presentation of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and weak light reflexes

shortlist.label: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with congenital muscular dystrophy, brain malformations, and occasionally ocular abnormalities, aligning with the case's findings of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and mild optic nerve pallor

shortlist.label: Baraitser-Winter syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by brain malformations, ocular abnormalities, and intellectual disability, which could explain the case's microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and weak light reflexes

shortlist.label: Cobblestone lissencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Involves brain malformations and ocular abnormalities, consistent with the case's prenatal and postnatal findings of microcephaly and ventricular enlargement

raw.rationale: The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, along with the ocular findings of weak light reflexes, mild optic nerve pallor, and a faint reddish tone of the fundus, are consistent with Walker-Warburg syndrome, a disorder characterized by brain and eye malformations.

rejected.label: Muscle-eye-brain disease
rejected.why: While it shares some similarities with Walker-Warburg syndrome, the specific combination of brain and eye findings in this case, particularly the severe thinning of certain brain lobes and the absence of notable muscular dystrophy symptoms, makes Walker-Warburg syndrome a more fitting diagnosis.

rejected.label: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy
rejected.why: This condition primarily presents with muscular dystrophy symptoms and less pronounced brain malformations compared to Walker-Warburg syndrome, which does not align well with the prominent brain and eye findings in this case.

rejected.label: Baraitser-Winter syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by a distinct set of craniofacial features and brain anomalies, Baraitser-Winter syndrome does not specifically match the combination of severe brain lobe thinning and the particular ocular findings described in this case.

rejected.label: Cobblestone lissencephaly
rejected.why: This condition is part of a spectrum of disorders that include Walker-Warburg syndrome but is more specifically characterized by a 'cobblestone' appearance of the brain surface due to lissencephaly, which is not explicitly mentioned in the case description.
